title: AJOP-T: A High-Order Hardening Law for Continuous Teardrop Bounding Surface Plasticity
content: We propose AJOP-T, a high-order hardening law within the continuous teardrop bounding surface framework for clays — rate-independent, without fractional or viscoplastic elements. It replaces the constant compression slope of bounding surface hardening with a derivative hierarchy from the Arc Joint via Optimum Parameters (AJOP) compression map. Teardrop geometry, plastic potential, mapping rule and SMP transformed stress are inherited unchanged; only the hardening law is reformulated, through the zeroth-order compression mapping, first-order tangent modulus and second-order curvature measure. The consistency condition yields an explicit hardening denominator and an elasto-plastic tangent where the compression law's stress dependence appears analytically. Five structural results are established: limit theorems identifying the constant-slope law as the architecture's high-stress asymptotic member; a closed-form boundary of the admissible hardening domain; SMP-invariance of the hierarchy; exact recovery of Phonchamni et al.'s refined consolidation settlement equation under isotropic normally consolidated loading; and emergence of a curved critical state line carrying a bounded, stress-level-dependent undrained strength ratio — a falsifiable low-stress prediction. Dimensionless response maps visualize the nonlinear structure; the compression map is anchored to high-pressure Boom Clay oedometer data, and a three-clay validation program, with undrained triaxial tests on two clays, pairs constant-slope and AJOP simulations on identical parameters.
